source.authors: Ohishi N, Hoshika N, Takeda M, Shibata K, Yamane H, Yokota T, Asahina M
source.title: Involvement of Auxin Biosynthesis and Transport in the Antheridium and Prothalli Formation in Lygodium japonicum

value: protonema length with 10 uM ABA added to GA4-methyl ester medium was 78.02 +/- 10.79 um (N = 76), about 50% of the GA4-Me-alone control
method: dark-grown protonema measured after culture on GA4-Me medium with and without ABA
conditions: Dark-germinated spores on Murashige and Skoog medium (0.5% agar, pH 5.5) at 25 C: 2-5 days in darkness, 24 h red light to trigger germination, then 7 more days in darkness; every Figure 2 treatment contained GA4-methyl ester (100 nM in the Results text) and the comparison is against GA4-Me alone, so the paper has no GA-free control in this figure; hormone concentrations are inconsistent inside the paper (Results text 10 uM ABA and 10 uM IAA; Methods sentence 100 uM for ABA and IAA); Steel-Dwass test, p < 0.05 (N = 60 GA alone, 76 GA + ABA, 44 GA + IAA); Methods state at least three independent samples; GA4-Me-alone protonema averaged 146.6 +/- 21.7 um (N = 60); the text reports ABA altered tissue morphology (Figure S1); two sentences later say antheridia still formed on some protonema whose elongation was restricted, which the authors read as antheridium formation not being directly suppressed by ABA.
where: Results 2.1, sentence citing Figures S1 and 2A
quote: As a result, 10 µM ABA drastically altered the tissue morphology (Figure S1), with the protonema length being reduced to 78.02 ± 10.79 µm (N = 76) (Figure 2A), approximately 50% of the control (GA4-Me alone).
note: Hormone-response experiments on cultured Lygodium japonicum protonema (GA4-Me, ABA, IAA applied in the medium).
